title: Spikes, firing rates and inter-spike intervals
description: Spike trains, rasters, firing rates, inter-spike interval distributions and the coefficient of variation; Poisson spiking as a descriptive baseline.

title: Descriptive, mechanistic and normative models
description: The 'what', 'how' and 'why' model types: what each explains, what it assumes, which questions it can answer and what evidence would count against it.

title: Leaky integrate-and-fire neuron
description: Membrane equation with leak, threshold, reset and refractory period; response to constant and stochastic input; firing-rate formula; what the model omits.

title: Tuning curves and neural encoding
description: Firing rate as a function of a stimulus variable, parametric tuning-curve models (Gaussian, von Mises), Poisson variability of counts, and the difference between synthetic and recorded tuning data.

title: Least-squares model fitting
description: Mean squared error, the closed-form least-squares estimator, design matrices, multiple and polynomial regression.

title: Maximum likelihood estimation
description: Probabilistic models of data, likelihood and log-likelihood, the MLE and its relation to least squares under Gaussian noise, weighted least squares and Poisson likelihoods.

title: Bootstrap and confidence intervals
description: Resampling with replacement to estimate the sampling variability of an estimator; percentile intervals; what the bootstrap assumes and where it fails.

title: Model selection, bias–variance and cross-validation
description: Training versus test error, the bias–variance decomposition, k-fold cross-validation and information criteria for choosing model complexity.

title: Poisson generalised linear models for encoding
description: The linear–nonlinear–Poisson model: exponential nonlinearity, Poisson log-likelihood, gradient and concavity, temporal receptive fields and their interpretation.

title: Logistic regression for decoding
description: Logistic regression as a GLM, cross-entropy loss, decoding behavioural variables from population activity, evaluation against chance and baselines.

title: Regularisation and sparsity
description: L2 and L1 penalties as priors, shrinkage and sparsity, choosing the penalty by cross-validation, effects on interpretation of fitted weights.

title: Principal component analysis
description: Orthonormal bases and projections, the sample covariance and its eigendecomposition, variance explained, reconstruction error and the limits of variance as a measure of relevance.

title: Nonlinear embeddings for visualisation
description: t-SNE and related methods for two-dimensional visualisation: what they preserve, what they distort, and how to read them.

title: Deep networks for decoding and encoding
description: Multilayer and convolutional networks as decoders of neural responses and as normative encoding models; training, evaluation and interpretation.

title: Linear and stochastic dynamical systems
description: Linear ODE systems and their eigen-solutions, Markov processes, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process and autoregressive models for neural signals.

title: Rate models and Wilson–Cowan dynamics
description: Population rate equations, fixed points and stability, excitatory–inhibitory networks and their phase-plane analysis.

title: Bayesian inference and decisions
description: Priors, likelihoods and posteriors for binary and continuous hidden states; loss functions and optimal decisions; fitting Bayesian observer models to behaviour.

title: Hidden dynamics: HMMs and the Kalman filter
description: Sequential probability ratio test, hidden Markov models and the Kalman filter as inference about latent states from noisy observations.

title: Reinforcement learning
description: Prediction with temporal-difference learning, bandits and exploration, Q-learning and model-based planning as models of learning.

title: Causality in neural networks
description: Interventions versus correlations, simultaneous regression and instrumental variables for inferring connectivity, and why decoding is not causation.
